title: Tail bound for low degree
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a real-valued function on the uniform Boolean cube, and let $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k>0$. Suppose every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is supported on a set of size at most $k$, and $\|f\|_2>0$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$ such that $(\sqrt{2e})^k\le t$, we have $\Pr\bigl(t\|f\|_2\le |f|\bigr)\le \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{k}{2e}t^{2/k}\right)$.
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most a positive integer $k$, with $\|f\|_2>0$. For $t\ge(\sqrt{2e})^k$, $\Pr(|f|\ge t\|f\|_2)\le\exp(-kt^{2/k}/(2e))$.
